meta.title: Global wind power 1980-2025 (country capacity, milestones, farms)
meta.based_on: wind-history-map v3 dataset, TW/JP-audited atlas v3 (see sources / notes)
edits: TWN 2005–2025 onshore/offshore = MOEA Energy Administration, Energy Statistics Handbook 2025, Table 3-6 (official annual table; 2025: 930.3 / 3,586.9 MW). The original map derived onshore as IRENA total minus a differently scoped offshore series, which put 2,064 MW 'onshore' in 2023.

JPN 2011–2025 = JWPA year-end cumulative installed capacity (2025: 6,434.2 MW); offshore = JWPA full offshore + semi-offshore/port sites (2025: 253.4 + 34.2 MW). The original map used IRENA (2025: 6,249 MW).
Farm 'Tomamae Winvilla' (JPN): end 2023 (repowered Oct 2023; GEM lists the repowered phase)

TWN/JPN farm audit: 9 farms re-classified (construction / retired / unverified); partly grid-connected Taiwanese offshore farms enter the operating layer in their full-completion year (Yunlin 2025, Greater Changhua 1&2a and Changfang & Xidao 2024); Hai Long 2&3, Greater Changhua 2b&4 and Taipower Offshore Phase 2 are listed as under construction at end-2025; Kitakyushu Hibikinada and the Goto floating farm are under construction (JWPA: no new offshore project in 2025).
Milestone 'Formosa 2': year 2021 -> 2023, text aligned with first power 2022/07, COD 2023/09

milestones.name: Brush wind turbine, Cleveland
milestones.en: First automatically operated wind turbine to generate electricity, a 12 kW, 144-blade machine charging batteries at Charles Brush's Cleveland mansion.
milestones.zh: 第一部自動運轉的發電用風力機：12 kW、144 片葉片，為 Charles Brush 位於克里夫蘭的宅邸蓄電池充電。

milestones.name: Balaklava WIME D-30 (Yalta)
milestones.maker: Soviet Union (TsAGI / Yuri Kondratyuk design team)
milestones.en: A 100 kW, 30 m rotor turbine near Yalta was the world's first utility-scale, grid-connected wind turbine feeding an AC network.
milestones.zh: 位於雅爾達附近的 100 kW、30 m 葉輪風機，是世界第一部併入交流電網的公用事業級風力機。

milestones.name: Smith–Putnam turbine, Grandpa's Knob, Vermont
milestones.maker: S. Morgan Smith Co. / Palmer Putnam
milestones.en: First megawatt-class wind turbine in the world (1.25 MW, 53 m two-blade rotor), feeding the Vermont grid until a blade failed in 1945.
milestones.zh: 全球第一部百萬瓦級風力機（1.25 MW、53 m 雙葉葉輪），併入佛蒙特電網運轉至 1945 年葉片斷裂為止。

milestones.name: Gedser wind turbine
milestones.en: The 200 kW Gedser turbine established the three-blade, upwind, stall-regulated 'Danish concept' that became the template for modern turbines.
milestones.zh: 200 kW 的 Gedser 風機確立三葉片、迎風、失速調節的「丹麥概念」，成為現代風力機的原型。

milestones.name: NASA/DOE MOD-0, Plum Brook Station, Ohio
milestones.en: First of the US federal MOD series test turbines (100 kW, 38 m), launching modern large-turbine R&D in the United States.
milestones.zh: 美國聯邦 MOD 系列試驗風機的第一部（100 kW、38 m），開啟美國現代大型風機研發。

milestones.name: Tvind turbine (Tvindkraft), Ulfborg
milestones.en: Volunteer-built 2 MW, 54 m turbine that was the largest in the world when completed and demonstrated fibreglass blades and downwind design; still operating.
milestones.zh: 由志工建造的 2 MW、54 m 風機，完工時為全球最大，驗證了玻纖葉片與順風設計，至今仍在運轉。

milestones.name: NASA/DOE MOD-1, Boone, North Carolina
milestones.en: First multi-megawatt (2 MW, 61 m) wind turbine of the modern era; its low-frequency noise problems shaped later siting and design practice.
milestones.zh: 現代第一部多百萬瓦級（2 MW、61 m）風力機；其低頻噪音問題影響了後續選址與設計。

milestones.name: Crotched Mountain wind farm, New Hampshire
milestones.en: Twenty 30 kW turbines on Crotched Mountain formed the world's first multi-turbine wind farm.
milestones.zh: Crotched Mountain 的二十部 30 kW 風機構成世界第一座多機組風場。

milestones.name: NASA/DOE MOD-2 cluster, Goodnoe Hills, Washington
milestones.en: Three Boeing MOD-2 turbines (2.5 MW, 91 m each) formed the first cluster of multi-megawatt machines and the largest turbines built to that date.
milestones.zh: 三部 Boeing MOD-2（各 2.5 MW、91 m）組成第一個多百萬瓦級機組群，也是當時所建最大的風機。

milestones.name: Altamont Pass wind farm, California
milestones.maker: U.S. Windpower, Fayette, Flowind and others
milestones.en: Start of the California wind rush: Altamont Pass grew to thousands of turbines and about 550 MW by the late 1980s, the world's largest concentration of wind power.
milestones.zh: 加州風電熱潮的起點：Altamont Pass 至 1980 年代末擴增至數千部風機、約 550 MW，為當時全球最大的風電聚落。

milestones.name: Growian, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Koog
milestones.en: Germany's 3 MW, 100 m rotor Growian was the largest turbine of its day; its structural failures pushed Germany toward smaller, incremental designs.
milestones.zh: 德國 3 MW、100 m 葉輪的 Growian 是當時最大的風機；其結構失效促使德國轉向較小型、漸進式的設計路線。

milestones.name: Muppandal wind farm (first phase), Tamil Nadu
milestones.maker: Tamil Nadu Energy Development Agency / NEPC, Suzlon and others
milestones.en: Beginning in 1986, the Aralvaimozhi pass at Muppandal became India's largest onshore wind cluster, exceeding 1,500 MW and anchoring Tamil Nadu's wind industry.
milestones.zh: 自 1986 年起，Muppandal 的 Aralvaimozhi 山口發展為印度最大的陸域風電聚落，超過 1,500 MW，支撐坦米爾納德邦的風電產業。

milestones.name: Vindeby offshore wind farm
milestones.en: Eleven 450 kW Bonus turbines off Lolland formed the world's first offshore wind farm, operating until 2017.
milestones.zh: Lolland 外海十一部 450 kW Bonus 風機組成世界第一座離岸風場，運轉至 2017 年。

milestones.name: Delabole wind farm, Cornwall
milestones.en: The United Kingdom's first commercial wind farm, ten 400 kW Vestas turbines in Cornwall.
milestones.zh: 英國第一座商業風場，位於康瓦爾的十部 400 kW Vestas 風機。

milestones.name: Enercon E-66 (first units), Emden / Aurich
milestones.en: Enercon's E-66 (1.5 MW, 66 m, gearless direct-drive) pioneered the megawatt-class direct-drive turbine that dominated the German 1990s boom.
milestones.zh: Enercon E-66（1.5 MW、66 m、無齒輪直驅）開創百萬瓦級直驅風機，主宰 1990 年代德國的風電熱潮。

milestones.name: Vestas V66 prototype, Tjæreborg
milestones.en: The Vestas V66-1.65 MW brought pitch-regulated, variable-slip 'OptiSlip' technology to the MW class and became the workhorse of late-1990s wind farms.
milestones.zh: Vestas V66-1.65 MW 將可變槳距與 OptiSlip 滑差技術帶入百萬瓦級，成為 1990 年代末風場的主力機型。

milestones.name: Dabancheng wind farm, Xinjiang
milestones.maker: Xinjiang Wind Energy Co. / Goldwind (technology origin)
milestones.en: China's first large wind farm (over 100 MW by 2000) and the birthplace of Goldwind, China's pioneering turbine manufacturer.
milestones.zh: 中國第一座大型風場（2000 年超過 100 MW），也是中國先驅風機製造商金風科技的發源地。

milestones.name: Middelgrunden offshore wind farm, Copenhagen
milestones.maker: Bonus Energy / Middelgrunden Wind Turbine Cooperative & Copenhagen Energy
milestones.en: Twenty 2 MW turbines in a curved row off Copenhagen, the world's largest offshore wind farm when built and a landmark of community co-ownership.
milestones.zh: 哥本哈根外海弧形排列的二十部 2 MW 風機，建成時為全球最大離岸風場，也是社區共同持有的典範。

milestones.name: Horns Rev 1
milestones.en: Eighty Vestas V80 turbines in the North Sea made Horns Rev 1 the first large-scale offshore wind farm and the first in true open-sea conditions.
milestones.zh: 北海的八十部 Vestas V80 風機使 Horns Rev 1 成為第一座大型離岸風場，也是第一座真正處於外海環境的風場。

milestones.name: Enercon E-126, Emden (Rysumer Nacken)
milestones.en: The Enercon E-126 (initially 6 MW, uprated to 7.58 MW, 127 m rotor, 135 m hub) was the world's most powerful wind turbine for nearly a decade.
milestones.zh: Enercon E-126（初期 6 MW，後提升至 7.58 MW，127 m 葉輪、135 m 輪轂高）近十年間為全球功率最大的風機。

milestones.name: Hywind Demo, Karmøy
milestones.en: The world's first full-scale floating wind turbine, a spar-buoy in 220 m of water off Karmøy, proved floating wind was technically feasible.
milestones.zh: 全球第一部全尺寸浮動式風力機，於 Karmøy 外海 220 m 水深的單柱浮筒平台上運轉，證明浮動式風電技術可行。

milestones.name: Jiuquan (Gansu) Wind Power Base
milestones.maker: State Grid / Longyuan, Huaneng, Datang and others
milestones.en: The Jiuquan base in the Gobi desert, begun in 2009, grew past 8 GW to become the world's largest onshore wind farm complex.
milestones.zh: 位於戈壁沙漠的酒泉風電基地自 2009 年起建，容量突破 8 GW，成為全球最大的陸域風電基地。

milestones.name: Donghai Bridge offshore wind farm, Shanghai
milestones.maker: Sinovel SL3000 / Shanghai Donghai Wind Power
milestones.en: China's first commercial offshore wind farm, 34 Sinovel 3 MW turbines beside the Donghai Bridge, launched the Chinese offshore industry.
milestones.zh: 中國第一座商業離岸風場，東海大橋旁的 34 部華銳 3 MW 風機，開啟中國離岸風電產業。

milestones.name: London Array
milestones.en: At 630 MW London Array was the world's largest offshore wind farm from 2013 to 2017, showing gigawatt-scale offshore was within reach.
milestones.zh: 630 MW 的 London Array 在 2013 至 2017 年間為全球最大離岸風場，證明 GW 級離岸風電已可企及。

milestones.name: Hywind Scotland, Buchan Deep
milestones.en: Five 6 MW spar-type turbines off Peterhead formed the world's first commercial floating wind farm.
milestones.zh: Peterhead 外海五部 6 MW 單柱式浮動風機組成全球第一座商業浮動式離岸風場。

milestones.name: Borssele / Hollandse Kust Zuid (zero-subsidy tenders)
milestones.en: Hollandse Kust Zuid, awarded subsidy-free in 2018 and fully commissioned in 2023, is the first offshore wind farm built without price support and the largest in the Dutch North Sea (1.5 GW).
milestones.zh: Hollandse Kust Zuid 於 2018 年以零補貼得標、2023 年全數完工，是第一座不靠價格補貼興建的離岸風場，也是荷蘭北海最大風場（1.5 GW）。

milestones.name: Formosa 1 offshore wind farm, Miaoli
milestones.maker: Ørsted, JERA, Macquarie, Swancor / Siemens Gamesa SWT-6.0-154
milestones.en: Taiwan's first commercial offshore wind farm (two 4 MW pilot turbines in 2017, 20 more 6 MW units in 2019), the starting point of Taiwan's offshore programme.
milestones.zh: 台灣第一座商業離岸風場（2017 年兩部 4 MW 示範機、2019 年再增 20 部 6 MW），是台灣離岸風電計畫的起點。

milestones.name: Hornsea 2
milestones.en: At 1,320 MW, Hornsea 2 became the world's largest operating offshore wind farm when fully commissioned in 2022.
milestones.zh: 1,320 MW 的 Hornsea 2 於 2022 年全數併網後成為全球最大運轉中的離岸風場。

milestones.name: Formosa 2 offshore wind farm, Miaoli
milestones.maker: JERA, Macquarie, Swancor / Siemens Gamesa SG 8.0-167 DD
milestones.en: Taiwan's first large-scale (376 MW) offshore wind farm to be fully commissioned: first power in July 2022, all 47 turbines in commercial operation in September 2023, marking the step from pilot projects to utility-scale build-out.
milestones.zh: 台灣第一座全數完工商轉的大型（376 MW）離岸風場：2022 年 7 月首度併網、2023 年 9 月 47 部機組全數商轉，標誌台灣從示範計畫邁向公用事業規模建置。

milestones.name: Dogger Bank A (Haliade-X 13 MW)
milestones.maker: SSE Renewables, Equinor, Vårgrønn / GE Vernova Haliade-X 13 MW
milestones.en: First power in October 2023 from GE's Haliade-X 13 MW turbines; Dogger Bank (3.6 GW across A/B/C) is the world's largest offshore wind project under construction.
milestones.zh: 2023 年 10 月 GE Haliade-X 13 MW 風機首度發電；Dogger Bank（A/B/C 合計 3.6 GW）為全球最大興建中離岸風電計畫。

milestones.name: Vestas V236-15.0 MW prototype, Østerild
milestones.en: The V236-15.0 MW prototype at Østerild set a world record for single-turbine daily output (363 MWh) and became the reference turbine for 2020s offshore projects.
milestones.zh: Østerild 的 V236-15.0 MW 原型機締造單機日發電量世界紀錄（363 MWh），成為 2020 年代離岸風場的參考機型。

milestones.name: Greater Changhua 1 & 2a offshore wind farm
milestones.en: Ørsted's 900 MW Greater Changhua 1 & 2a, completed in 2024 about 35-60 km off Changhua, was Taiwan's largest offshore wind farm when completed.
milestones.zh: 沃旭能源 900 MW 的大彰化東南及西南第一階段風場於 2024 年完工，距彰化外海約 35–60 km，完工時為台灣最大的離岸風場。

milestones.name: Vineyard Wind 1, Massachusetts
milestones.maker: Avangrid & Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners / GE Vernova Haliade-X 13.6 MW
milestones.en: The first commercial-scale offshore wind farm in the United States (806 MW), delivering first power to the New England grid in January 2024.
milestones.zh: 美國第一座商業規模離岸風場（806 MW），2024 年 1 月首度向新英格蘭電網送電。

milestones.name: Mingyang MySE 18.X-20 MW, Hainan
milestones.en: Mingyang's 18-20 MW platform with a 260-292 m rotor, installed at Hainan in 2024, is the most powerful wind turbine ever built.
milestones.zh: 明陽智能 18–20 MW 平台、260–292 m 葉輪，2024 年於海南安裝，是史上功率最大的風力機。

milestones.name: Dongfang 26 MW offshore turbine, Fujian
milestones.en: Dongfang Electric's 26 MW, 310 m rotor turbine, rolled out in 2024 and installed for testing in 2025, pushes single-turbine capacity past the 25 MW mark.
milestones.zh: 東方電氣 26 MW、310 m 葉輪風機於 2024 年下線、2025 年安裝測試，使單機容量突破 25 MW。

early: DNK 1980-1999, DEU 1990-1999, NLD 1990-1999 are taken directly from official national statistics (via Wikipedia). DNK values rounded to integer MW.

USA: 1981-1990 driven by California (CEC: ~10 MW 1981, ~240 MW 1983, ~610 MW 1984, ~945 MW 1985, ~1,500 MW 1990); ~30-50 MW elsewhere. 1991-1997 nearly flat with retirements (AWEA/EIA ~1,610-1,710 MW). 1998 (~1,820) and 1999 (~2,500) reflect the PTC-driven 1998-99 boom.

DEU 1983-1989, NLD 1981-1989, GBR 1988-1991, ESP 1985-1991, IND 1985-1989, SWE 1982-1990, CHN 1986-1994, GRC 1982-1991, JPN 1990-1994, BEL 1986-1994, AUS 1987-1994: interpolated/estimated between sparse anchor points (demonstration turbines and first commercial projects); treat as approximate (+/-50%).
ESP 1999: BTM Consult revised figure 1,812 MW; EWEA's provisional figure was ~1,540 MW.
IND: MNES reports on fiscal-year (March) basis; values shifted to nearest calendar year-end.
MEX: La Venta I (1.6 MW, 1994) only. EGY: Hurghada demonstration site (~5 MW) only. ISR: Golan Heights (Ma'ale Gilboa) ~6 MW from 1992. TUR: Alacati (7.2 MW) + Germiyan (1.5 MW), 1998.
MAR and TWN omitted: Morocco's first farm (Koudia Al Baida, 50 MW) and Taiwan's first commercial turbines (Mailiao, 2.6 MW) were both commissioned in 2000; pre-2000 capacity was <1 MW of test units.

Implied world totals: ~10 MW (1980), ~1,050 MW (1985), ~2,040 MW (1990), ~4,900 MW (1995), ~7,700 MW (1997), ~13,800 MW (1999), consistent with BTM/EWEA world totals (~1,020 / ~1,930 / ~4,780 / ~7,600 / ~13,600 MW) within the uncertainty of the estimated series.
offshore: 2016-2025 values for all countries except CHN and VNM are taken verbatim from the Wikipedia 'Offshore wind power' capacity-by-country table (WFO reports: fully commissioned farms). GWEC world totals are higher (57.2 GW 2021, 64.3 GW 2022, 75.2 GW 2023, 83.2 GW 2024, 92.5 GW 2025) because GWEC counts installed/partially commissioned capacity and China/Vietnam differently.

CHN 2021-2025 use China NEA/GWEC grid-connected cumulative figures rather than the WFO/Wikipedia series (19,747/26,563/31,527/38,283/42,315): 2021 26,390 (NEA; consistent with GWEC ~17 GW added in 2021 and Asia 49.5% of 56 GW), 2022 30,510 (NEA), 2023 ~37,290 (approx, NEA), 2024 ~41,270 (approx), 2025 48,400 (GWEC GOWR 2026). 2023-2024 values are from memory of NEA releases and are approximate (+/- ~0.5 GW).

CHN 2007-2015 from GWEC/CWEA: Bohai Suizhong 1.5 MW demo 2007; 2009 23 MW; 2010 150 (Donghai Bridge 102 + Rudong intertidal); 2011 258; 2012 390; 2013 429; 2014 658; 2015 1,015. 2011 and 2009 are least certain.

VNM: Bac Lieu phase 1 16 MW (2013); 99 MW at 2015 (Bac Lieu phase 2 completed around Jan 2016, GWEC lists 99 MW; year of 83 MW step uncertain, could be 2016); 2021 = 99 + 779 MW intertidal/nearshore installed in 2021 per GWEC; 2022-2025 ~900-1,000 MW are approximate GWEC-style nearshore totals (WFO/Wikipedia instead give 396 for 2022 and 496 for 2023-2025).

Pre-2016 European values: built from EWEA per-country tables (2013, 2015 verbatim; 2014 = 2015 minus EWEA 2015 annual additions: UK 4,494, DE 1,013, NL 247, SE 212) and from farm commissioning dates for earlier years, checked against the EWEA cumulative European total per year (1993:5, 1994:7, 1995:12, 1996:29, 1998:32, 2000:36, 2001:86, 2002:256, 2003:532, 2004:622, 2005:712, 2006:804, 2007:1,122, 2008:1,496, 2009:2,073, 2010:2,956, 2011:3,829, 2012:4,995, 2013:6,562, 2014:8,008, 2015:11,027). Our per-country sums match these within ~1% each year except 2009 (sum 2,109 vs 2,073).

Farms used for interpolation: DNK Vindeby 4.95 (1991), Tuno Knob 5 (1995), Middelgrunden 40 (2000), Horns Rev I 160 (2002), Nysted 166 + Samso 23 + Ronland 17 + Frederikshavn 11 (2003), Horns Rev II 209 + Sprogo 21 + Avedore 7 (2009), Rodsand II 207 (2010), Anholt 400 (2012 part/2013 full); NLD Lely 2 (1994), Irene Vorrink 17 (1996), Egmond aan Zee 108 (2007), Prinses Amalia 120 (2008), Luchterduinen 129 + Westermeerwind part (2015), Gemini 600 (2016); SWE Bockstigen 2.75 (1998), Utgrunden 10.5 (2000), Yttre Stengrund 10 (2001, decommissioned 2015), Lillgrund 110 (2007), Vanern 30 (2009), Karehamn 48 (2013); GBR Blyth 4 (2000), North Hoyle 60 (2003), Scroby Sands 60 (2004), Kentish Flats 90 (2005), Barrow 90 (2006), Burbo Bank 90 + Beatrice demo 10 (2007), Lynn & Inner Dowsing 194 (2008), Rhyl Flats 90 + Gunfleet Sands (2009), Robin Rigg 180 + Thanet 300 (2010), Walney 1 + Ormonde + Sheringham part (2011), Walney 2 + Greater Gabbard + Sheringham (2012), London Array 630 + Lincs 270 + Teesside 62 (2013), West of Duddon Sands 389 (2014), Gwynt y Mor 576 + Humber Gateway 219 + Westermost Rough 210 (2015); DEU Emden 4.5 (2004), Breitling 2.5 (2006), Hooksiel 5 (2008), Alpha Ventus 60 (2009), Baltic 1 48 (2011), BARD 1 400 (2011-2013), Riffgat/Meerwind/Nordsee Ost/DanTysk (2014), 2015 wave incl. Global Tech I, Borkum Riffgrund 1, Butendiek, Amrumbank, Baltic 2, Trianel; BEL Thornton Bank I 30 (2008/09), Belwind 165 (2010), Thornton Bank II 185 (2012), Thornton Bank III + Northwind part (2013), Northwind 216 (2014); FIN Kemi Ajos 24 offshore turbines (2008), Pori demo 2.3 (2010), Tahkoluoto 42 (2017); IRL Arklow Bank 25 (2004); NOR Hywind demo 2.3 (2009), Hywind Tampen 88 (2023); PRT WindFloat 1 2 MW (2011-2016), WindFloat Atlantic 25 (2020); ESP Arinaga 5 (2013); JPN Setana 1.2 + Sakata 10 (2004), Kamisu 1 14 (2010), Kamisu 2 16 + Choshi 2.4 + Kitakyushu 2 + Fukushima 2 (2013), Fukushima 7 (2015), Fukushima 5 (2016); KOR Woljeong test bed 5 (2012), Tamra 30 (2016); USA Block Island 30 (2016), CVOW pilot 12 (2020), South Fork 132 (2024); TWN Formosa 1 phase 1 8 (2017), Formosa 1 128 (2019), Changhua demo 109 (2021), Formosa 2 376 (2023), Greater Changhua 1&2a 900 + others (2024), Yunlin 640 (2025); ITA Taranto 30 (2022).

DNK 2004-2008 held at 426 (farm sum); EWEA reported 409 MW for those years (differences in how Ronland/Frederikshavn are counted). DNK 2009-2011 (663/870/871) are farm sums; EWEA reported 664/854/857.
GBR 2008 uses EWEA 591 (Lynn & Inner Dowsing partially grid-connected at year end) rather than farm sum 598.
DEU 2010-2012 (92/200/280) are EWEA year-end grid-connected figures and include partially connected farms (Baltic 1, BARD Offshore 1).
SWE excludes the 0.22 MW Nogersund/Svante 1 turbine (1990-2007). JPN 2004-2009 value of 11 MW counts Sakata (10 MW, nearshore/breakwater) and Setana (1.2 MW).
KOR: Wikipedia/WFO series shows a drop from 136 (2020) to 104 (2021); kept as published. FIN and SWE small declines 2017-2019 reflect decommissioning/recounting in the WFO series.
farms: Year = year of full commissioning where available; for farms commissioned across a year boundary the completion year is used.

Coordinates are approximate farm centres (+/-0.1 deg). Where the Wikipedia country table gave none or gave an implausible value (e.g. Borkum Riffgrund 2 listed at 54.97N), centre was estimated from the farm's known location/description.

Dogger Bank A (GBR): first power Oct 2023, full commissioning 2025 -> year=2025. Sofia (GBR): first power Aug 2025, completion expected 2026 -> year=2025 flagged; exclude if strict full-commissioning is required.

Moray West, Neart na Gaoithe (GBR), Borkum Riffgrund 3, He Dreiht (DEU), Calvados, Yeu-Noirmoutier, EFGL, EolMed (FRA), Vineyard Wind 1 (USA) all reached full commissioning in 2025 (partial generation in 2024 for some), so they are excluded from end-2024 totals. Vineyard Wind 1 first power Jan 2024.
Beatrice Demonstrator (GBR, 2x REpower 5M, 2007) is recorded with end=2024 (decommissioning of the demo turbines); verify if needed. Blyth Offshore (2000) decommissioned 2019.
Hooksiel (DEU) 1x BARD 5 MW nearshore test turbine (2008): status uncertain (reported dismantled ~2019); no end year recorded.
Bockstigen (SWE) original 1998 turbines were replaced in 2018 (5 x Vestas V47); shown as one continuously operating farm.
Kemi Ajos (FIN) listed as original 30 MW (2008); Wikipedia Baltic list reports 38 MW after turbine changes. Pori Tahkoluoto includes the 2010 2.3 MW demo turbine.
SeaMade (BEL) split into Seastar (252 MW) and Mermaid (235 MW); Vesterhav (DNK) split into Nord and Syd; Hollandse Kust Zuid split into I&II and III&IV; Gode Wind split into 1 and 2.

Lake/inland-water farms included because national statistics count them: Vindpark Vänern (SWE), Lely, Irene Vorrink, Westermeerwind, Windpark Fryslân (NLD, IJsselmeer). Netherlands total may differ by ~100 MW depending on treatment of these and of HKZ nominal (1,540) vs installed (1,529) capacity.
Robin Rigg (GBR) capacity shown as 174 MW (58 turbines) after removal of 2 turbines in 2015; originally 180 MW.
Belwind's Alstom Haliade 6 MW demonstrator (2013) recorded separately from Belwind I (165 MW).

Estimated coordinates (no explicit source coordinates): Blyth Offshore, Blyth Demonstrator, Galloper, Kentish Flats Extension, Trianel Borkum II, Kaskasi, Nordergründe, Deutsche Bucht, Arcadis Ost 1, Baltic Eagle, Gode Wind 3, Borkum Riffgrund 3, He Dreiht, all Belgian farms, all Dutch farms, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian, Norwegian, US farms, Vesterhav Nord/Syd, Sofia, Dogger Bank A.

Not included (not commissioned by end-2025): Hornsea 3, Inch Cape, Dogger Bank B/C, Thor, Baltic Power (POL), Revolution Wind, CVOW Commercial, Sunrise Wind, Empire Wind, Dieppe-Le Tréport, Hollandse Kust West, Ecowende, Nordseecluster.
year = year of first grid connection (full commissioning may be later; see note fields).

China: English Wikipedia list only has 20 farms >=100 MW; 4C Offshore reports 181 operating farms in China but its data are paywalled and Chinese portals (bjx.com.cn, zhihu) block fetching. Farms not in Wikipedia were compiled from NEA/CWEA-reported project names known to the compiler; coordinates for these are placed off the named county coast (±0.2°) and flagged 'coords approximate'. Rows tagged 'identity uncertain' or 'aggregate placeholder' should be verified against 4C Offshore / GEM Global Wind Power Tracker before publication.

China provincial cumulative grid-connected offshore capacity (21jingji, Sep 2024): Jiangsu >10 GW, Guangdong >10 GW (together 58.1% of 39.1 GW national), Shandong >5 GW, Zhejiang >4.7 GW, Fujian >3.7 GW, Tianjin+Hebei+Liaoning+Shanghai+Guangxi 1.53 GW combined; national 39.1 GW end Q3 2024, ~41.3 GW end 2024.

Taiwan: capacities are full build-out; Yunlin (640), Greater Changhua 1&2a (900), Changfang&Xidao (589) were grid-connected in stages 2021/2022-2024, so 'year' undercounts lag if you count full MW in the first year. Reference end-2024 cumulative 2137 MW (GWEC-style fully commissioned) vs ~3.0 GW if all partially-connected farms are counted in full.
Japan: Fukushima FORWARD (14 MW floating) decommissioned 2021; Setana/Sakata early port turbines are marginal 'offshore'. Reference end-2024 346 MW.
Korea: reference end-2024 212 MW includes small test units (Woljeong, Ulsan floating).

Vietnam: all farms are intertidal/nearshore (monopile in <5 m water) in the Mekong Delta; many 30-50 MW farms were rushed to the Oct-2021 FiT deadline. Capacities for several small farms are best-estimate.
India and other Asian countries: no operational offshore wind farms through 2025.
Floating demos are typed 'floating'; fixed-bottom farms typed 'offshore'.
Coordinates are site-level (approx. +/-0.02 deg), assigned from township/industrial-park location; not from a GIS source.

Taipower fleet cross-check: the 15 pre-2022 Taipower sites listed here sum to 168 turbines and ~299.8 MW vs. the official 168 turbines / 297.04 MW (Feb 2022); the ~2.8 MW gap is most likely in the Datan 1.5/2.0 MW unit split or derated units.

Four Taipower sites that appear on the 2025 live dashboard but post-date the 2022 figure (Longmen, Taixi, Yongxing, Luzhu; 19 turbines) have ESTIMATED capacities (~4.2 MW class, 2.3 MW for Longmen) and years; they are marked in each record's note. Taipower's 2025 onshore target was 370 MW, consistent with ~70 MW of additions.
wpd (ex-InfraVest 英華威) figures are from wpd's own project list; the 'Houlong' record aggregates Houlong + Tongxiao/Yuanli (通苑) sites and the 'Changbin Lukang' record includes Lunwei (崙尾).

Not included (not operating or unverified): Far Eastern Group's Zhufeng (竹風) Zhubei project (blocked, not commissioned), Dongcheng (東成) proposal, and any Formosa Plastics expansions beyond the 2000 demo units.
zh.wikipedia and MOEA Energy Administration statistics pages were not reachable from this environment; owner/turbine details rely on the sources above plus well-known public records.

Cumulative check (sum of listed farms by commissioning year): 42.6 MW by 2005, 552 MW by 2010, 655 MW by 2015, 655 MW by 2020, 858 MW by 2025. Official Taiwan wind totals: ~647 MW end-2015 (all onshore), ~726 MW onshore end-2020, ~900+ MW onshore end-2024. The 2015 figure matches; the ~70 MW gap in 2020 reflects small/self-use sites and repowering not captured here.

Coverage: major operational onshore farms (generally >= ~200 MW) plus the 3-10 largest and/or historic first farms for each listed country. Aggregated 'bases'/corridors (Hami, Jiuquan, Markbygden, Muppandal, Jaisalmer, Jhimpir, Tehachapi, Altamont, San Gorgonio, Fosen) are flagged in 'note'.
'year' = commissioning of first phase; 'mw' = current aggregate capacity. Chinese base first-phase years are approximate (marked in note).

Several coordinates in the Wikipedia extract were hemisphere/longitude errors (e.g. Lagoa dos Ventos, Reynosa, Whitla, Gabal El Zeit, Cabo Leones, Noordoostpolder, Alxa Left Banner); they were corrected to the known site location. Every record whose coordinates were placed from region/township knowledge rather than a listed coordinate carries 'coordinates approximate' in note (typical accuracy +/-0.1 deg).

Farms from the Wikipedia list with implausible entries were dropped: 'Chu Se 700 MW', 'Hordavind 682 MW', 'Ventos de Santa Luzia 724.5 MW', Romanian 'Adamdel/Banca/Iberdrola Cogealac' (all sharing one central-Romania coordinate), 'Hopkins Ridge 385 MW' (actual ~157 MW). 'Aeolos' from the request could not be identified and is omitted.
Germany has no single very large onshore farm; the entries are the best-known clusters/historic parks with approximate aggregate capacities.
Offshore, nearshore/intertidal (e.g. Bac Lieu, Walney) and lake-based (Windpark Fryslan) farms are excluded, except the Noordoostpolder record which notes its nearshore component.
Non-English Wikipedias, GEM wiki, 4C and thewindpower.net country lists were not reachable from this environment; turbine details are from the sources above and public records, and may be incomplete.

[windfarmTaiwan edit] Formosa 2 milestone year set to 2023 (first power July 2022, all 47 turbines commercial September 2023, per the developers' releases); Greater Changhua 1&2a milestone reworded to 'largest when completed'.
audit: Taiwan 2005–2025 national onshore/offshore series is replaced directly from the MOEA Energy Administration annual table; the atlas no longer derives onshore capacity by subtracting a differently scoped offshore series.

Taiwan farm coverage counts full operating project nameplate only. Partly grid-connected projects can therefore appear in the official national offshore capacity before the full project marker enters the coverage layer.

Japan 2011–2025 total capacity is replaced with JWPA annual statistics. The 2019–2025 offshore series uses JWPA full offshore plus semi-offshore/port-accessible sites to remain consistent with the atlas broad offshore convention.

Japan 2024–2025 atlas offshore capacity of 287.6 MW combines JWPA full offshore 253.4 MW with 34.2 MW of semi-offshore sites last explicitly itemised by JWPA at end-2023; JWPA reported no new offshore project in 2025.
Construction, unverified, and future projects remain searchable but are excluded from operating farm coverage.
